Some of them say it is a solecism (laḥn), because only one object has come for «يحسبنّ»; among those who said this is Abū Ḥātim. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is weak, and he permitted it despite its weakness on the basis that the first object is omitted; the meaning according to him is: "let not those who disbelieve reckon themselves (إيّاهم) able to frustrate [Allah] in the earth", meaning "let them not reckon their own selves able to frustrate [Allah] in the earth".
I saw Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] incline to this view, I mean the view of al-Farrāʾ. And I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say about this reading: «الذي» [sic] is in the position of the accusative; he said: the meaning is: "let not the disbeliever reckon those who disbelieve able to frustrate [Allah] in the earth".

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
«يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِيَسْتَأْذِنْكُمُ الَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا الْحُلُمَ مِنْكُمْ ثَلاثَ مَرَّاتٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ صَلاةِ الْفَجْرِ وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيابَكُمْ مِنَ الظَّهِيرَةِ وَمِنْ بَعْدِ صَلاةِ الْعِشاءِ ثَلاثُ عَوْراتٍ لَكُمْ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلا عَلَيْهِمْ جُناحٌ بَعْدَهُنَّ طَوَّافُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ بَعْضُكُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ كَذلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآياتِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ» (58)
Al-Ḥasan read «وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا الْحُلُمَ» with the lām made quiescent [i.e. الحُلْم], because of the heaviness of the ḍamma. The Medinans and Abū ʿAmr read «ثَلاثُ عَوْراتٍ» in the nominative, and the Kufans read (ثلاث عورات) in the accusative; what is said about this is close to what is said about «يحسبنّ». Abū Ḥātim said: the accusative is weak and rejected. Al-Farrāʾ said: the nominative is dearer to me. He said: I chose the nominative only because the meaning is "these traits are three [times of] privacy". The nominative according to al-Kisāʾī is by being the mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) according to him is what follows it. He did not say [that it is nominative] by the returning pronoun; he stated explicitly: by being the mubtadaʾ. He said: the ʿawrāt are the hours in which there is exposure and privacy — yet he read it in the accusative. There are two views on the accusative: one of them is that it refers back to His words «ثَلاثَ مَرَّاتٍ» [as a badal (substitute)], and for this reason al-Farrāʾ considered it far-fetched. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is "let them ask your permission at the times of three [periods of] privacy". [Translator's note: the source announces two views on the accusative but only the first is explicitly numbered; al-Zajjāj's statement evidently represents the second.]
«طَوَّافُونَ» means "they are going round". Al-Farrāʾ said: as you say in ordinary speech: إنّما هم خدمكم وطوافون عليكم ("they are only your servants and those who go round among you"). Al-Farrāʾ ] permitted «طوافين» in the accusative [as a ḥāl (circumstantial)], because it is indefinite and the pronoun in «عليكم» is definite. The Basrans do not permit it to be a ḥāl from the pronoun from «الذين» [sic] in «عليكم» and in «بعضكم», because of the difference of the two governing words. It is not permissible [to say] مررت بزيد، ونزلت على عمرو العاقلين ("I passed by Zayd and stayed with ʿAmr, the two intelligent ones") as a naʿt (adjective) for both of them. [Translator's note: the source prints «نصب طوافون» with the nominative form and contains a stray bracket; the sentence on the pronoun is translated as written.]
«بَعْضُكُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ لله» [sic] is with an implied verb, i.e. "some of you go round to others". [Translator's note: the word «لله» after the Quranic phrase appears to be an intrusion in the printed text.]
«كَذلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآياتِ»: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. Allah makes clear to you His signs that indicate His oneness, with a making-clear like that by which He made these things clear to you.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: Al-Ḥasan read «الحلم» [i.e. الحُلْم], dropping the ḍamma because of its heaviness. «فَلْيَسْتَأْذِنُوا», i.e. let them ask permission at all times. He did not say فليستأذنوكم ("let them ask your permission"), whereas He said in the first [verse] «لِيَسْتَأْذِنْكُمُ», because children are not addressed and not charged with worship ...

nahhas-irab:60-60.t:
«وَالْقَواعِدُ مِنَ النِّساءِ» is the plural of قاعد, without the hāʾ [the feminine ending]. There are three views on it: the doctrine of the Basrans is that it is by way of attribution (nasab) [i.e. "one characterised by sitting"]; the doctrine of the Kufans is that since it is applied only to the feminine, it has no need of the hāʾ; and the third view is that it came without the hāʾ to distinguish it from القاعدة in the sense of "the one sitting down".
«فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِنَّ جُناحٌ أَنْ يَضَعْنَ ثِيابَهُنَّ غَيْرَ مُتَبَرِّجاتٍ بِزِينَةٍ» is as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they do not intend to display their adornment to men.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
«لَيْسَ عَلَى الْأَعْمى حَرَجٌ»: [«حرج»] is the noun (ism) of «ليس», and we have already mentioned it. Among the best of what has been said about it is that it concerns jihād. As for the meaning of «وَلا عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَنْ تَأْكُلُوا مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ آبائِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ» to the end of the verse, there are three views on it: one is that this is permissible only after permission; another is that it was known that they would not begrudge them this; and the third view is that the verse is abrogated, and that this was at first, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Your blood and your wealth are inviolable except with permission, and the inviolability of a Muslim's property is like the inviolability of his blood." From this it follows that nothing of anyone's property is lawful for anyone except with permission, or what the Muslims agree upon when one fears for one's life.
It has been said: the verse is abrogated by His words, Mighty and Majestic: «يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتاً غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا عَلى أَهْلِها» [al-Nūr: 27]; if one may not enter except with permission, then with food it is even further [from permissible]. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
«يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلى طَعامٍ غَيْرَ ناظِرِينَ إِناهُ» [al-Aḥzāb: 53]. Even if there were nothing on the abrogation of the verse except the ḥadīth that Mālik related from Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "None of you should milk his brother's livestock except with his permission. Would any of you like his storeroom to be come to, his store broken open and his food taken?" — that would suffice.
Qatāda read «مفتاحه» ("its key"), and it is a dialectal form; مفتح is more common in the speech of the Arabs, as is shown to you by its plural مفاتح.
«أَنْ تَأْكُلُوا جَمِيعاً»: [«جميعا»] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
«تَحِيَّةً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: because the meaning of «فَسَلِّمُوا»
is "greet". Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted «تحيّة» in the nominative, in the sense of "it is a greeting". «مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ»: because Allah commanded it. «مُبارَكَةً طَيِّبَةً»: because the one who hears it finds it pleasant to hear.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t:
«إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِذا كانُوا مَعَهُ عَلى أَمْرٍ جامِعٍ لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا حَتَّى يَسْتَأْذِنُوهُ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَأْذِنُونَكَ أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَإِذَا اسْتَأْذَنُوكَ لِبَعْضِ شَأْنِهِمْ فَأْذَنْ لِمَنْ شِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمُ اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ» (62)
«إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). «وَإِذا كانُوا مَعَهُ عَلى أَمْرٍ جامِعٍ», i.e. something in which nothing but gathering together is needed [sic], such as war and the like. [Translator's note: «ما يحتاج فيه إلا الاجتماع» is translated as written; the sense intended is presumably "something for which gathering together is needed".] «لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا حَتَّى يَسْتَأْذِنُوهُ», because he may need their presence.

nahhas-irab:63-63.t:
«لا تَجْعَلُوا دُعاءَ الرَّسُولِ بَيْنَكُمْ كَدُعاءِ بَعْضِكُمْ»: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a second object.
«قَدْ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ يَتَسَلَّلُونَ مِنْكُمْ لِواذاً»: [«لواذا»] is a maṣdar (verbal noun); it may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "taking cover with one another". Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: i.e. "going against [him]"; its real sense is that some of them take refuge (yalūdh) behind others, i.e. hide behind them so as not to be seen. One says لاوذ يلاوذ ملاوذة ولواذا, and لاذ يلوذ لوذا ولياذا: the wāw is changed to yāʾ because of the kasra before it, following لاذ in its weakness. When it is the maṣdar of fāʿala, it is not made weak, because fāʿala cannot be made weak.
«فَلْيَحْذَرِ الَّذِينَ يُخالِفُونَ عَنْ أَمْرِهِ أَنْ تُصِيبَهُمْ فِتْنَةٌ»: «أن» is in the position of the accusative by «يحذر». According to most grammarians حذر زيدا ("he was wary of Zayd") is not permissible, but with «أن» it is permissible, because prepositions are dropped with it. «عَنْ أَمْرِهِ أَنْ تُصِيبَهُمْ» [sic] is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). [Translator's note: this last statement is translated as printed; it does not fit the phrase quoted, and something appears to have dropped out of the source.]

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Nūr
Medinan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سُورَةٌ أنْـزَلْناها﴾ — the reading is with the nominative (rafʿ), and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read "سُورَةً" in the accusative (naṣb). As for the nominative, it is by an implied "هَذِهِ سُورَةٌ أنْزَلْناها" (this is a sūra which We have sent down); making it nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) is ugly, because it is indefinite, and "أنْزَلْناها" is a ṣifa (adjective) of it. The accusative is on two possibilities: with the meaning "أنْزَلْنا سُورَةً" (We sent down a sūra), just as you say "زَيْدًا ضَرَبْتُهُ" (Zayd, I struck him), and with the meaning "اُتْلُ سُورَةً أنْزَلْناها" (recite a sūra which We have sent down). ﴿وَفَرَضْناها﴾ is with the rāʾ unstressed, and it is also read with the rāʾ doubled (فَرَّضْناها). Whoever reads it unstressed, its meaning is "ألْزَمْناكُمُ العَمَلَ بِما فُرِضَ فِيها" (We have bound you to act upon what is ordained in it). Whoever reads it doubled, it is on two possibilities: one of them in the sense of multiplicity, meaning "إنّا فَرَضْنا فِيها فُرُوضًا كَثِيرَةً" (We have ordained many ordinances in it), and [the other] in the sense of "بَيَّنّا، وفَصَّلْنا" (We have made clear and set out in detail) what is in it of the lawful and the unlawful.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿الزّانِيَةُ والزّانِي فاجْلِدُوا كُلَّ واحِدٍ مِنهُما مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ﴾ — the reading is with the nominative (rafʿ), and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it in the accusative (naṣb): "اَلزّانِيَةَ والزّانِيَ", with fatḥa on the tāʾ. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh claimed that the accusative is the preferred [form], and Sībawayh claimed that the reading is the nominative; others among the Basrans and the Kufans claimed that the preferred [form] is the nominative, and so it is in my view, because the nominative is as if by consensus in the reading, and it is stronger in Arabic, since its meaning is the meaning of "مَن زَنى فاجْلِدُوهُ" (whoever commits fornication, flog him), so its interpretation is as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Sībawayh and al-Khalīl said that the nominative is in the sense of "وَفِيما فَرَضْنا عَلَيْكُمُ الزّانِيَةُ والزّانِي" (and among what We have ordained for you: the fornicatress and the fornicator), in the nominative, or "اَلزّانِيَةُ والزّانِي فِيما فُرِضَ عَلَيْكم" (the fornicatress and the fornicator, in what is ordained for you). The proof that the preferred [form] is the nominative is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واللَّذانِ يَأْتِيانِها مِنكم فَآذُوهُما﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 16]. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh only preferred the accusative because it is a command, and a command is more fitting with a verb. The accusative is permissible in the sense of "اِجْلِدُوا الزّانِيَةَ والزّانِيَ" (flog the fornicatress and the fornicator). The consensus is that flogging applies to those who are not muḥṣan (not married and chaste): the unmarried man and the unmarried woman are flogged one hundred lashes, and banishment goes together with the flogging in the view of many jurists: "he is flogged one hundred and exiled for a year"; as for the people of Iraq, they flog him one hundred.
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَأْخُذْكم بِهِما رَأْفَةٌ في دِينِ اللَّهِ﴾ — it is also read "رَآفَةٌ في دِينِ اللَّهِ", on the pattern of "رَعافَةٌ", and it is read "يَأْخُذْكم" with the yāʾ. "رَآفَةٌ" is like "اَلسَّآمَةُ", as in your saying "سَئِمْتُ سَآمَةً" (I grew weary, weariness), and like it is "كَآبَةٌ"; for "فَعالَةٌ" is among the noun-patterns of maṣdars (verbal nouns), and "سَآمَةٌ" is on the analogy of "كَلالَةٌ"; and "فَعالَةٌ" is used for qualities, such as "اَلْقَباحَةُ" (ugliness), "اَلْمَلاحَةُ" (comeliness) and "اَلْفَخامَةُ" (grandeur), and this is very frequent. The meaning of ﴿وَلا تَأْخُذْكم بِهِما رَأْفَةٌ في دِينِ اللَّهِ﴾ is: "do not have mercy on them so that you drop from them the ḥadd (prescribed punishment) that Allah has commanded"; and it was said: "[it means that] they are flogged severely". His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذابَهُما طائِفَةٌ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — the reading is with sukūn on the lām, and kasra on it is permissible. People differed about "الطّائِفَةُ" (a party): some of them said: one and above is a "طائِفَةٌ"; others said: a ṭāʾifa is not less than two; some of them said: three; some said: four; and some said: ten. As for whoever said "one", that is contrary to what the people of the language hold, because "اَلطّائِفَةُ" has the meaning of "اَلْجَماعَةُ" (a group), and the least of a group is two. The least that is required for a ṭāʾifa, in my view, is two, and what ought to be sought in witnessing the punishment of the fornicator is that they be a group, because what predominates in [the meaning of] ṭāʾifa is "اَلْجَماعَةُ" (a group).

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿الزّانِي لا يَنْكِحُ إلا زانِيَةً أوْ مُشْرِكَةً والزّانِيَةُ لا يَنْكِحُها إلا زانٍ أوْ مُشْرِكٌ﴾ — it is permissible to say "اَلزّانِي لا يُنْكَحُ إلّا زانِيَةً" and "اَلزّانِيَةُ لا يُنْكَحُها إلّا زانٍ", but it has not been read thus. [Translator's note: the forms are given as written in the source.] The interpretation of "اَلزّانِي لا يَنْكِحُ إلّا زانِيَةً" is in the sense of "لا يَتَزَوَّجُ" (he does not marry), and likewise "اَلزّانِيَةُ لا يَتَزَوَّجُها إلّا زانٍ" (none marries the fornicatress except a fornicator). Some people said that the meaning of nikāḥ here is intercourse, so the meaning according to them is: "the fornicator has intercourse only with a fornicatress, and none has intercourse with the fornicatress except a fornicator". This view is far-fetched, because nothing is known of the mention of nikāḥ in the Book of Allah except in the sense of marriage. Allah, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَأنْكِحُوا الأيامى مِنكم والصّالِحِينَ مِن عِبادِكم وإمائِكُمْ﴾ [al-Nūr: 32], and this is marriage without any doubt; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا نَكَحْتُمُ المُؤْمِناتِ ثُمَّ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 49], so He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the contract of marriage is called "اَلنِّكاحُ". Most of the exegesis holds that this verse was revealed concerning some poor Muslims who were in Medina and who intended to marry prostitutes who were in Medina, who committed fornication and took payment; they wanted to marry them so that the women would support them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down the prohibition of that. It was also said that they wanted to be indulgent with them, and they were informed that this is forbidden.
It is related that al-Ḥasan said: the fornicator, when the ḥadd (prescribed punishment) has been carried out on him, is married only to a woman on whom the ḥadd has been carried out like him; and likewise the woman, when the ḥadd has been carried out on her, according to him, is married only to a man like her. Some of them said: the verse is abrogated; it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿وَأنْكِحُوا الأيامى مِنكُمْ﴾ [al-Nūr: 32]. Most of the opinion is that the meaning here is marriage. It is permissible to say "وَحَرَّمَ ذَلِكَ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ" (and He forbade that to the believers), in the sense of "وَحَرَّمَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ" (and Allah forbade that to the believers), but it has not been read thus. This is a statement in wording, but its meaning is that of a command. Had it been as those who said it is intercourse claimed, there would be no benefit in the speech, because if the speaker says: the fornicatress fornicates only with a fornicator, and the fornicator fornicates only with a fornicatress, there is no benefit in it except by way of intensifying the matter, as you say of a man whom you have known for lying: "هَذا كَذّابٌ" (this one is a liar), intending to make his case grave. So according to what carries benefit, and what the language requires, the meaning is that of marriage.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم ورَحْمَتُهُ وأنَّ اللَّهَ تَوّابٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ — here the answer (jawāb) of "لَوْلا" is left out, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم لَنالَ الكاذِبُ لِما ذَكَرْنا عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ" (were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you, a great punishment would have befallen the liar for what We mentioned), and this is indicated by: ﴿وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم ورَحْمَتُهُ في الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ لَمَسَّكم في ما أفَضْتُمْ فِيهِ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ [al-Nūr: 14].

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ جاءُوا بِالإفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِنكُمْ﴾ — the meaning of "اَلْإفْكُ" here is the lie. Some of them have been named in the reports (āthār), but they were not named in the Qurʾān. Among those named are Ḥassān ibn Thābit, Misṭaḥ ibn Uthātha and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, and among the women Ḥamna bint Jaḥsh. ﴿لا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّا لَكم بَلْ هو خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ — it said "لَكم" (for you, plural), while the one who was targeted was ʿĀʾisha, may Allah have mercy on her; so it was said "لَكم", by which is meant: she and those connected with her, namely the Prophet ﷺ and Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him.
His saying: ﴿والَّذِي تَوَلّى كِبْرَهُ مِنهُمْ﴾, and it is also read "كُبْرَهُ مِنهم", ﴿لَهُ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾. Whoever reads "كِبْرَهُ", its meaning is: whoever took upon himself the sin in that; and whoever reads "كُبْرَهُ" means: the greater part of it. It is related that Ḥassān ibn Thābit came in to ʿĀʾisha, and it was said to her: Do you let in this man about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿والَّذِي تَوَلّى كِبْرَهُ مِنهم لَهُ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾? She said: "Has not his sight gone?" And it is related that he recited to her his saying in his verse:
؎حَصانٌ رَزانٌ ما تُزَنُّ بِرِيبَةٍ ∗∗∗ وتُصْبِحُ غَرْثى مِن لُحُومِ الغَوافِلِ
(Chaste, composed, never suspected of any doubt; she wakes hungry of the flesh of unwary women — i.e. she does not backbite them.)
She said to him: "But you are not like that." And His saying, Exalted is He: "والخامِسَةُ أنْ غَضَبُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها", with "أنَّ" lightened and "غَضَبُ" in the nominative, in the sense of "أنَّهُ غَضَبُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها" (that it is: the wrath of Allah be upon her); and it is permissible to say "أنْ غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْها" (that Allah is wroth with her). Here there is an implied (muḍmar) "hāʾ", and "أنْ" is lightened from the heavy one; the meaning is "أنَّهُ غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْها" and "أنَّهُ غَضَبُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها". [Translator's note: this discussion concerns al-Nūr: 9 and is placed here in the source.] The poet said:
؎فِي فِتْيَةٍ كَسُيُوفِ الهِنْدِ قَدْ عَلِمُوا ∗∗∗ أنْ هالِكٌ كُلُّ مَن يَحْفى ويَنْتَعِلُ
(Among young men like Indian swords, who knew that everyone who goes barefoot or shod will perish.)
It came in the exegesis concerning His saying ﴿لا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّا لَكم بَلْ هو خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ that by it are meant ʿĀʾisha and Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal; and "لَكم" may be in the sense of "لَكُما" (for you two). What we explained first includes the matter of ʿĀʾisha, Ṣafwān, the Prophet ﷺ, and everyone who had a connection with ʿĀʾisha; and it may be for everyone who was accused on account of [this matter].

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لَوْلا إذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ المُؤْمِنُونَ والمُؤْمِناتُ بِأنْفُسِهِمْ خَيْرًا﴾ — its meaning is: "هَلّا إذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ؟" (why, when you heard it, did not…?), because the meaning of "ظَنَّ المُؤْمِنُونَ بِأنْفُسِهِمْ" is in place of an allusion to them and to some of them; and likewise it is said of people some of whom kill others: "إنَّهم يَقْتُلُونَ أنْفُسَهم" (they kill themselves). ﴿وَقالُوا هَذا إفْكٌ مُبِينٌ﴾, that is: a manifest lie.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ المُحْصَناتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِأرْبَعَةِ شُهَداءَ فاجْلِدُوهم ثَمانِينَ جَلْدَةً﴾ — the meaning of "يَرْمُونَ المُحْصَناتِ" is: [accuse them] of fornication; but He did not say "بِالزِّنا" (of fornication), because in the preceding mention of the fornicatress and the fornicator there is an indication that this is the meaning. The position of "اَلَّذِينَ" is nominative (rafʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject). On the reading of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, the position of "اَلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ المُحْصَناتِ" must be accusative (naṣb), in the sense of "اِجْلِدُوا الَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ المُحْصَناتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِأرْبَعَةِ شُهَداءَ" (flog those who accuse chaste women and then do not bring four witnesses), and on that is the preference of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl. "اَلْمُحْصَناتُ" here are the women who have guarded their private parts through chastity.
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْبَلُوا لَهم شَهادَةً أبَدًا وأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾ ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وأصْلَحُوا﴾ [al-Nūr: 5] — people differed about accepting the testimony of the slanderer (al-qādhif). Some of them said: if he repents of his slander, his testimony is accepted; and it is related that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb accepted the testimony of two slanderers, and said to Abū Bakra: "If you repent, I will accept your testimony"; and his repentance is that he retract the slander. This is the position of most jurists. As for the people of Iraq, they say: his testimony is not accepted, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَلا تَقْبَلُوا لَهم شَهادَةً أبَدًا﴾. They said: and His saying ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وأصْلَحُوا فَإنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [al-Nūr: 5] — they said: this exception is from His saying ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾, so those who repent are excepted from the transgressors. Those who claimed that his testimony is accepted said: the exception is from His saying ﴿وَلا تَقْبَلُوا لَهم شَهادَةً أبَدًا﴾ — ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا﴾ [al-Nūr: 5]; they said: and His saying ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾ is a description of them. They agreed by consensus that whoever slandered while a disbeliever, then embraced Islam and repented, and was upright after his Islam, his testimony is accepted, even though he was a slanderer. Analogy requires accepting the testimony of the slanderer if he repents; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says regarding testimonies: ﴿مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ الشُّهَداءِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 282], and the slanderer is not graver in crime than the disbeliever, so it is his due that, if he repents and makes amends, his testimony be accepted, just as the disbeliever, if he embraces Islam and makes amends, has his testimony accepted.
If someone says: then what is the benefit of His saying "أبَدًا" (ever)? It is said: the benefit is that "ever" for every person is the extent of his span in his life, and the extent of his span in what is connected with his case. So you say: "اَلْكافِرُ لا يُقْبَلُ مِنهُ شَيْءٌ أبَدًا" (nothing is ever accepted from the disbeliever), and its meaning is: "as long as he remains a disbeliever, nothing is accepted from him". Likewise when you say: "اَلْقاذِفُ لا تُقْبَلُ مِنهُ شَهادَةٌ أبَدًا" (no testimony is ever accepted from the slanderer), its meaning is: "as long as he remains a slanderer". So when disbelief departs from him, his "ever" has departed; and likewise the slanderer, when the slander departs from him, his "ever" has departed from him, and there is no difference between this and that. It is also read: "ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِأرْبَعَةٍ شُهَداءَ", with tanwīn, ﴿فاجْلِدُوهُمْ﴾; so "أرْبَعَةٍ" is genitive (makhfūḍ) with tanwīn, and "شُهَداءَ" is a ṣifa (adjective) of "أرْبَعَة", in the position of the genitive (jarr). It may also be in the position of the accusative (naṣb) from two angles: one of them in the sense of "ثُمَّ لَمْ يُحْضِرُوا أرْبَعَةً شُهَداءَ" (then they did not bring forward four witnesses), and [the other] as the accusative of ḥāl (circumstantial) with an indefinite: then they did not come in the state of [being] witnesses. As for ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا﴾ [al-Nūr: 5], it may be in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ and mīm (in «لَهُمْ»), in the sense of "وَلا تَقْبَلُوا لَهم شَهادَةً أبَدًا إلّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا" (and do not ever accept testimony from them, except those who repent); and it may be in the position of the accusative as an exception, upon His saying ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾ ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا﴾ [al-Nūr: 5]. And if they are excepted from the transgressors as well, then acceptance of their testimony becomes obligatory, because the name of transgression has departed from them.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أزْواجَهم ولَمْ يَكُنْ لَهم شُهَداءُ إلا أنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: "والَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أزْواجَهم بِالزِّنا" (and those who accuse their wives of fornication).
His saying: ﴿فَشَهادَةُ أحَدِهِمْ أرْبَعُ شَهاداتٍ بِاللَّهِ﴾ — it is also read "أرْبَعَ شَهاداتٍ بِاللَّهِ" in the accusative (naṣb). Whoever reads "أرْبَعُ" in the nominative (rafʿ), it is as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject); the meaning is: "the testimony of one of them which wards off the ḥadd of the slanderer is four", and the proof of that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَدْرَأُ عَنْها العَذابَ أنْ تَشْهَدَ أرْبَعَ شَهاداتٍ بِاللَّهِ﴾ [al-Nūr: 8]. Whoever puts "أرْبَعًا" in the accusative, the meaning is: "فَعَلَيْهِمْ أنْ يَشْهَدَ أحَدُهم أرْبَعَ شَهاداتٍ" (it is upon them that one of them testify four testimonies), and in the sense of "فالَّذِي يَدْرَأُ عَنْها العَذابَ أنْ يَشْهَدَ أحَدُهم أرْبَعَ شَهاداتٍ" (what wards off the punishment from her is that one of them testify four testimonies). [Translator's note: the source has «عَنْها» here, although the context concerns the husband's testimony.]

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿والخامِسَةُ أنَّ لَعْنَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾ — it is permissible to say "والخامِسَةَ أنَّ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ", and likewise "والخامِسَةُ أنَّ غَضَبَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها" and "اَلْخامِسَةَ", both. Whoever says "والخامِسَةَ" (accusative), it is in the sense of "وَيَشْهَدُ الخامِسَةَ" (and he testifies the fifth). When the slanderer accuses his wife, his testimony is that he say: "أشْهَدُ بِاللَّهِ إنِّي لَمِنَ الصّادِقِينَ فِيما قَذَفْتُها بِهِ" (I testify by Allah that I am among the truthful in what I accused her of), or he says: "أحْلِفُ بِاللَّهِ إنِّي لَمِنَ الصّادِقِينَ فِيما قَذَفْتُها بِهِ" (I swear by Allah that I am among the truthful in what I accused her of), four times; and he says in the fifth: "لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إنْ كانَ مِنَ الكاذِبِينَ" (the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars). Likewise the woman says: "أشْهَدُ بِاللَّهِ إنَّهُ لَمِنَ الكاذِبِينَ فِيما قَذَفَنِي بِهِ" (I testify by Allah that he is among the liars in what he accused me of), four times, and she says in the fifth: "وَعَلَيَّ غَضَبُ اللَّهِ إنْ كانَ مِنَ الصّادِقِينَ" (and upon me be the wrath of Allah if he is among the truthful). This is the liʿān (mutual imprecation). When they have performed the mutual imprecation, they are separated, and she observes the waiting period (ʿidda) of a divorced woman from that moment. When they have done that, he may never marry her, in the view of most jurists of the people of the Ḥijāz, and some of the Kufans follow them, namely Abū Yūsuf. Analogy is what the people of the Ḥijāz hold, because the slanderer accused her of fornication, and it is not fitting for him to marry a fornicatress, and no repentance becomes apparent for this. The liʿān takes place only before a judge from among the judges of the Muslims.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿إذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ بِألْسِنَتِكُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: when some of you cast it to others. ʿĀʾisha, may Allah have mercy on her, read: "إذْ تُلْيِقُونَهُ بِألْسِنَتِكم" [Translator's note: so in the source; the reading attributed to ʿĀʾisha is usually given as «تَلِقُونَهُ», from وَلَقَ يَلِقُ], and its meaning is: "when you hasten with the lie". It is said "وَلَقَ، يَلِقُ" when someone hastens in lying and other things. The poet said:
؎جاءَتْ بِهِ عَنْسٌ مِنَ الشّامِ تِلْقْ
(A sturdy she-camel brought him from Syria, going swiftly.)
That is: hastening.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا يَأْتَلِ أُولُو الفَضْلِ مِنكم والسَّعَةِ﴾ — it was also read: "وَلا يَتَألَّ أُولُو الفَضْلِ مِنكم والسَّعَةِ". The meaning of "تَأْتَلِي" is: to swear, and likewise "يَتَألّى" means: he swears. The meaning of ﴿أنْ يُؤْتُوا﴾ is "ألّا يُؤْتُوا أُولِي القُرْبى" (that they will not give to the near of kin); the meaning is: "let not those of you possessed of bounty and means swear that they will not give to the near of kin and the needy". This verse was revealed concerning Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq; he had sworn that he would not bestow his bounty upon Misṭaḥ ibn Uthātha — who was the son of his maternal aunt — because of his reviling ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her. When ﴿ألا تُحِبُّونَ أنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾ was revealed, Abū Bakr said: "Yes indeed", and he restored his bounty to Misṭaḥ and to whomever he had sworn not to bestow upon, and he made expiation for his oath. [Translator's note: Misṭaḥ is usually described as the son of Abū Bakr's maternal cousin; the source says «ابْنَ خالَتِهِ».]
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ المُحْصَناتِ الغافِلاتِ المُؤْمِناتِ لُعِنُوا في الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ﴾ [al-Nūr: 23] — it was said that by it are meant the wives of the Prophet ﷺ; and it was said that its origin is the matter of ʿĀʾisha, and then it became [applicable] to everyone who accuses believing women. He did not say here "والمُؤْمِنِينَ" (and the believing men), dispensing with it because whoever accuses a believing woman must inevitably accuse a believing man together with her; so He dispensed with mentioning the believing men, because mention of the believing men and believing women has already occurred, and His mention of the believing women indicates the believing men. Just as He said: ﴿سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 81] and did not say "وَتَقِيكُمُ البَرْدَ" (and protect you from cold), because what protects from heat protects from cold, so He dispensed with mentioning one of them by means of the other.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ الحَقَّ﴾ — it is also read "اَلْحَقُّ" (nominative). Whoever reads "اَلْحَقُّ", then "اَلْحَقُّ" is a description of "اَللَّهُ", Mighty and Majestic is He, and the meaning is: "يَوْمَئِذٍ يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللَّهُ الحَقُّ دِينَهم" (on that day Allah, the Truth, will pay them their due in full). Whoever reads "دِينَهُمُ الحَقَّ", then "اَلْحَقَّ" is a description of "الدِّين", and "الدِّين" here is the recompense; the meaning is: "يَوْمَئِذٍ يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللَّهُ جَزاءَهُمُ الحَقَّ" (on that day Allah will pay them in full their true recompense), that is: "جَزاءَهُمُ الواجِبَ" (their due recompense).

zajjaj:26-26.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿الخَبِيثاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ والخَبِيثُونَ لِلْخَبِيثاتِ والطَّيِّباتُ لِلطَّيِّبِينَ والطَّيِّبُونَ لِلطَّيِّباتِ﴾ — there are two possibilities in it. The meaning is: "the foul words are for the foul among men, and the foul men are for the foul words", that is: none speaks foul [words] except the foul among men and women, and none speaks good [words] except the good among men and women. It is also possible that the meaning is that these foul words cleave only to the foul among men and the foul among women; as for the pure, good women, nothing cleaves to them. It was also said: the foul among women are for the foul among men, and likewise the good among women are for the good among men.
His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ مُبَرَّءُونَ مِمّا يَقُولُونَ﴾, that is: ʿĀʾisha and Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal; and likewise everyone of the believing men and believing women who is slandered is declared innocent of what the foul slanderers say. ﴿لَهم مَغْفِرَةٌ ورِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾, that is: for those who were slandered and accused there is forgiveness and a noble provision, and for the slanderers there is the curse in this world and the Hereafter, and a great punishment.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾ — it is read with ḍamma (بُيُوتًا) and with kasra (بِيُوتًا), but the ḍamma is more common. Whoever gives it ḍamma does so according to the basic form of the plural: "بَيْتٌ" is pluralized "بُيُوتٌ", like "قَلْبٌ" and "قُلُوبٌ", and "فَلْسٌ" and "فُلُوسٌ". Whoever reads with kasra only puts kasra because of the yāʾ that comes after the bāʾ, and that, in the view of the Basrans, is very poor, because there is no "فِعُولٌ" with kasra on the fāʾ [of the pattern] in the speech of the Arabs. [Translator's note: the source writes «فَعُولٌ» while describing a pattern with kasra on the fāʾ.]
His saying: ﴿حَتّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا وتُسَلِّمُوا عَلى أهْلِها﴾ — the meaning of "تَسْتَأْنِسُوا" in the language is: you ask permission, and so it is in the exegesis. "اَلِاسْتِئْذانُ" (asking permission) is seeking to know: you say "آذَنْتُهُ بِكَذا", that is: I informed him; and likewise "آنَسْتُ مِنهُ كَذا وكَذا": I came to know such-and-such from him; and likewise ﴿فَإنْ آنَسْتُمْ مِنهم رُشْدًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 6], that is: you come to know. So the meaning of "حَتّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا" is: until you seek to know whether its occupants want to let [you] in or not. The proof that it is permission is His saying: ﴿فَإنْ لَمْ تَجِدُوا فِيها أحَدًا فَلا تَدْخُلُوها حَتّى يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ﴾ [al-Nūr: 28].

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكم جُناحٌ أنْ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ مَسْكُونَةٍ فِيها مَتاعٌ لَكُمْ﴾, that is: "there is no blame on you in entering these without permission". It came in the exegesis that the khāns (inns) are meant by it; a khān is called "فُنْدُقٌ" and "فُنْتُقٌ", with dāl and with tāʾ. It was said "there is no blame on you in entering these houses" only because He had forbidden entering houses that are not theirs except with permission; so they were informed that entering these permitted places — such as inns and trading shops in which things are sold and whose owners permit entering them — is allowed. It was also said that by it are meant the ruins which a man enters to urinate or relieve himself, and the meaning of "فِيها مَتاعٌ لَكم" is then in the sense of "إمْتاعٌ" (benefit), that is: you find relief in them from what afflicts you.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إلا ما ظَهَرَ مِنها﴾, that is: they should not display their hidden adornment, such as the necklace, the anklet, the armlet and the bracelet; and that which is shown is the clothes and the face.
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلا يَضْرِبْنَ بِأرْجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعْلَمَ ما يُخْفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّ﴾ — a woman would sometimes pass by with an anklet on her foot, and sometimes there would be several anklets on it; when she struck with her foot, it would be known that she was wearing anklets and adornment, and this stirs desire, so it was forbidden, just as they were commanded not to display [their adornment], because hearing its sound is equivalent to displaying it.

zajjaj:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأنْكِحُوا الأيامى مِنكم والصّالِحِينَ مِن عِبادِكم وإمائِكُمْ﴾ — it was also read "مِن عَبِيدِكم", and both are permissible. This is binding with regard to the unmarried (al-ayāmā), and the meaning is: "and marry off the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male and female slaves, if they [the women] desire chastity".
The meaning of ﴿وَلا تُكْرِهُوا فَتَياتِكم عَلى البِغاءِ إنْ أرَدْنَ تَحَصُّنًا﴾ [al-Nūr: 33] is: "do not compel them to prostitution at all"; the meaning is not: "do not compel them if they desire chastity, and if they do not desire it, then it is not for us to compel them". [Translator's note: so in the source.]
His saying: ﴿إنْ يَكُونُوا فُقَراءَ يُغْنِهِمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ — so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, urged marriage and made known that it is a means of removing poverty. It is related from ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "I marvel at a man, how he does not desire marriage, when Allah says: ﴿إنْ يَكُونُوا فُقَراءَ يُغْنِهِمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾".

zajjaj:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَبْتَغُونَ الكِتابَ مِمّا مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم فَكاتِبُوهم إنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا﴾ — concerning the meaning of ﴿إنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا﴾ it was said: "if you know [them capable of] paying what they are released upon", that is: "you know that they can earn what they will pay". [Translator's note: the source has «يَكْتِبُونَ», apparently for «يَكْسِبُونَ» (earn); translated according to the evident sense.] The meaning of mukātaba (manumission contract) is that a man contracts with his male or female slave, on condition of releasing him, that when he pays him such-and-such an amount of money in such-and-such instalments, the slave is free once he has paid everything owed; and his walāʾ (clientage) belongs to his master who contracted with him, because his master was generous to him with the earnings which originally belong to his master.
His saying: ﴿وَآتُوهم مِن مالِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي آتاكُمْ﴾ — this, in the view of most jurists, is a recommendation: that the master give him something from what he is releasing him upon, or from his own wealth, something by which he can be helped to settle his instalments; and he may refrain from doing so. Likewise he may contract with him when he requests the mukātaba, and he may refrain from contracting with him. The form of this command is the form of permission, as He said: ﴿وَإذا حَلَلْتُمْ فاصْطادُوا﴾ [al-Māʾida: 2], because He had forbidden them hunting as long as they were in iḥrām; and likewise His saying: ﴿فَإذا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلاةُ فانْتَشِرُوا في الأرْضِ وابْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Jumuʿa: 10] — this is after He had forbidden them trading at the time of the call to prayer. So He permitted it here because the owned slave has no property and has power over nothing, so Allah permitted them to give him power [to earn]. It is related from ʿUmar that he contracted with a slave of his whose kunya was "Abū Umayya", and he was the first slave given a mukātaba in Islam. He brought him the first instalment, and ʿUmar handed it back to him and said: "Seek help with it for your mukātaba." He said: "If only you had deferred it until the last instalment." He said: "I fear that I will not live to see that."
His saying: ﴿أوْ نِسائِهِنَّ﴾ [al-Nūr: 31] — that is because it is not lawful for polytheist women to see of believing women what it is lawful for believing women to see; by "their women" are meant the women of the believers, and the believing men and believing women are allies of one another.
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهُنَّ أوِ التّابِعِينَ غَيْرِ أُولِي الإرْبَةِ﴾ [al-Nūr: 31] — "غَيْرِ" is a ṣifa (adjective) of "اَلتّابِعِينَ", an indication [of what is meant] in His saying ﴿أوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهُنَّ﴾ [al-Nūr: 31]; its meaning too is: "غَيْرِ أُولِي الإرْبَةِ مِنَ الرِّجالِ" (other than those men possessed of desire). The meaning is: "they should not display their adornment to their slaves or to their followers, unless they are without desire". "اَلْإرْبَةُ" is need, and its meaning here is: those without need of women. As for the genitive of "غَيْرِ", it is a ṣifa of "اَلتّابِعِينَ"; although "غَيْر" is used to describe an indefinite, "the followers" here does not refer to particular people; its meaning is only: for every follower without desire. It is also permissible to say "غَيْرَ", with "غَيْرَ" in the accusative, in two ways: one of them is exception, the meaning being: "they should not display their adornment except to the followers, except those possessed of desire, for they should not display their adornment to them"; and it may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), so that the meaning is: "and the followers, not desiring women", that is: in this state.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أوِ الطِّفْلِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلى عَوْراتِ النِّساءِ﴾ [al-Nūr: 31] — it is also read "عَوَراتِ", with fatḥa on the wāw, because "فَعْلَةٌ" is pluralized on "فَعَلاتٌ", with fatḥa on the ʿayn, as in your saying "جَفْنَةٌ" and "جَفَناتٌ", "صَحْفَةٌ" and "صَحَفاتٌ". But when it is like your saying "لَوْزَةٌ", "جَوْزَةٌ" and "عَوْرَةٌ", the more common [practice] is to give it sukūn — and likewise His saying "بَيْضاتٌ" [Translator's note: so in the source, «قَوْلُهُ»] — because of the heaviness of the vowel with the wāw and the yāʾ. Among the Arabs are those who keep to the base form and analogy in this, and say "جَوَزاتٌ" and "بَيَضاتٌ", and on this "عَوَراتِ" was read. The meaning of "لَمْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلى عَوْراتِ النِّساءِ" is: they have not reached [the age] where they are capable of women, as you say "قَدْ ظَهَرَ فُلانٌ عَلى فُلانٍ" (so-and-so has prevailed over so-and-so) when he has become strong enough for him. And "لَمْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلى عَوْراتِ النِّساءِ" may mean: "they do not know the shamefulness of women's private parts as distinct from other [parts]".

zajjaj:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أنْـزَلْنا إلَيْكم آياتٍ مُبَيِّناتٍ﴾ — it is read with fatḥa and with kasra. Whoever reads "مُبَيَّناتٍ" with fatḥa, the meaning is that there is no ambiguity in them; and whoever reads with kasra, the meaning is that they make clear to you the lawful from the unlawful.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He has made clear the whole matter of the heaven and the matter of the earth, with a luminous clarification beyond whose light there is no further limit, and He said: ﴿اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, that is: "the Disposer of their affair with far-reaching wisdom and luminous proof". Then He gave a likeness of that light of His in the hearts, by the clearest light that is not perceived by the eyes, and said: ﴿مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكاةٍ فِيها مِصْباحٌ﴾. His light may be what we mentioned of His disposing; it may be His Book by which He made [things] clear, as He said: ﴿قَدْ جاءَكم مِنَ اللَّهِ نُورٌ وكِتابٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 15]; and it may be that the Prophet ﷺ is the light of which He said "مَثَلُ نُورِهِ", because the Prophet ﷺ is the guide, the one who makes clear, and the one who transmits from Allah what is luminous and clear. He said: ﴿كَمِشْكاةٍ﴾, which is the niche (kuwwa); it was said that it is in the language of the Abyssinians, but "اَلْمِشْكاةُ" is of the speech of the Arabs. Like it — even though it is used for something other than the niche — is "اَلشَّكْوَةُ", which is well known: it is the small «الدَّقِيقُ» [Translator's note: so in the source; probably «الزِّقُّ» (waterskin) is intended — the shakwa is a small waterskin], or what is made like it. ﴿فِيها مِصْباحٌ المِصْباحُ في زُجاجَةٍ﴾ — "اَلْمِصْباحُ" is the lamp. He said "اَلْمِصْباحُ في زُجاجَةٍ" because the light in glass and the brightness of fire is clearer in it than in anything else, and its brightness increases in glass. Then He described the glass and said: ﴿كَأنَّها كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ﴾; "دُرِّيٌّ" is a relative adjective (nisba), [meaning] that it is like pearls (al-durr) in its clarity and beauty. It was also read "دِرِّيٌّ" and "دَرِّيٌّ", with kasra and with fatḥa, and it has been transmitted with hamza; all the grammarians do not know a valid way for it [with ḍamma and hamza], because there is nothing in the speech of the Arabs on the pattern "فُعِّيلٌ". But kasra with hamza is good: it would be on the pattern "فِعِّيلٌ", and would come from the brilliant stars (al-darārī) that "tadra'" (تَدْرَأُ), that is: descend and travel thrusting along. [Translator's note: the source has «تَدَرُ» here.] "دِرِّيٌّ" without hamza may be lightened from this. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: It is not permissible to give the dāl ḍamma and also use hamza, because there is no "فُعِّيلٌ" in the language; the pattern of "دُرِّيٌّ" is "فُعْلِيٌّ", a nisba to "اَلدُّرُّ" (pearls). Whoever gives the dāl kasra says "دِرِّيٌّ", and he may use hamza or not. Whoever uses hamza takes it from "دَرَأ، يَدْرَأُ الكَوْكَبُ", when the star thrusts along shooting down so that its brightness is multiplied; it is said "تَدارَأ الرَّجُلانِ" when the two men push against each other; and its pattern is "فِعِّيلٌ". Whoever gives it kasra [without hamza], its origin is with hamza which was lightened, and the kasra of the dāl remained as it originally was, and its pattern is also "فِعِّيلٌ", as it was when it had hamza.
His saying: ﴿يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ﴾ — it is also read "تُوقَدُ" with the tāʾ. Whoever reads with the yāʾ means the lamp, which is masculine; and whoever reads with the tāʾ means the glass. "في زَجاجَةٍ" with fatḥa on the zāy is also permissible [Translator's note: the source has «زَجاحَةٍ», evidently a misprint]. There are two other ways in it which have been read: "تَوَقَّدُ", with fatḥa and with ḍamma on the dāl, and with the qāf doubled in both. Whoever reads "تَوَقَّدُ", the meaning is: "the glass is kindled"; and whoever reads "تَوَقَّدَ" gives it fatḥa because it is a past verb, and the meaning is: "the lamp is in a glass; the lamp was kindled".
His saying: ﴿مِن شَجَرَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ﴾ — there is nothing among trees whose branch bears leaves from its beginning to its end like the olive and the pomegranate. The poet said:
؎بُورِكَ المَيْتُ الغَرِيبُ كَما ∗∗∗ بُورِكَ نَظْمُ الرُّمّانِ والزَّيْتُونِ
(Blessed be the dead man far from home, as the rows of pomegranate and olive are blessed.)
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا شَرْقِيَّةٍ ولا غَرْبِيَّةٍ﴾ — most of the exegesis holds that it is not among those on which the sun rises only at the time of its rising, or only at setting; that is, nothing screens it at any time of the day, that is: it is both eastern and western, that is: the sun strikes it morning and evening, which makes it more flourishing and better for its oil and its olives. Al-Ḥasan said: the interpretation of His saying ﴿لا شَرْقِيَّةٍ ولا غَرْبِيَّةٍ﴾ is that it is not of the trees of this world, that is: it is of the trees of Paradise.

zajjaj:36-36.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِي بُيُوتٍ أذِنَ اللَّهُ أنْ تُرْفَعَ﴾ — it came in the exegesis: "أنْ تُبْنى" (that they be built); and al-Ḥasan said: the interpretation of "أنْ تُرْفَعَ" is "أنْ تُعَظَّمَ" (that they be honoured). "في" is attached (min ṣilat) to His saying "كَمِشْكاةٍ"; the meaning is: "like a niche in houses", that is: in mosques; and al-Ḥasan said: by it is meant Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). It is also possible that "في" is connected to "يُسَبِّحُ", and that "فِيها" is a repetition for the sake of tawkīd (emphasis), so that the meaning is: "men glorify Allah in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised". It is also read "يُسَبَّحُ لَهُ فِيها" (passive), and then the nominative of "رِجالٌ" here is as an explanation of the passive verb (lit. "that whose agent is not named"); the meaning is that when He said "يُسَبَّحُ لَهُ فِيها" (He is glorified therein), it is as though it were asked: "Who glorifies Allah?", and it was said: "men glorify [Him]", as the poet said:
؎لِيُبْكَ يَزِيدٌ ضارِعٌ لِخُصُومَةٍ ∗∗∗ ومُخْتَبِطٌ مِمّا تُطِيحُ الطَّوائِحُ
(Let Yazīd be wept for — [let] one humbled in a dispute [weep], and one seeking favour, of those whom calamities have cast away.)
"اَلْآصالُ": its singular is "أُصُلٌ", and they are the evenings.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
The meaning of ﴿لا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجارَةٌ ولا بَيْعٌ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وإقامِ الصَّلاةِ وإيتاءِ الزَّكاةِ﴾ is: no matter distracts them from that. It is related that Ibn Masʿūd saw some people of the market; the call to prayer had been made, and they left their trading and rose to the prayer, and he said: "These are among those of whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿رِجالٌ لا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجارَةٌ ولا بَيْعٌ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾."
His saying: ﴿وَإقامِ الصَّلاةِ وإيتاءِ الزَّكاةِ﴾ — the [normal] expression is "أقَمْتُ الصَّلاةَ إقامَةً" (I established the prayer, an establishing), and its origin is "أقَمْتُ إقْوامًا", but the wāw was likewise changed [into alif], so two alifs came together, and one of them was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, leaving "أقَمْتُ الصَّلاةَ إقامَةً"; and the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) was introduced as compensation for what was dropped. Here the iḍāfa (genitive construct) takes the place of the dropped hāʾ in compensating, and this is agreed upon by the grammarians.
His saying: ﴿يَخافُونَ يَوْمًا تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ القُلُوبُ والأبْصارُ﴾ — "تَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ القُلُوبُ والأبْصارُ" is permissible outside the Qurʾān, but "تَقَلَّبُ" is not permissible in the Qurʾān, because the reading is a sunna (established practice) which is not to be contravened, even if that is permissible in Arabic. The meaning of "تَتَقَلَّبُ" is: they quake and tremble from alarm and fear. Its meaning is that whoever's heart was certain of the resurrection and the Rising will increase in insight and will see what he loves of what he was promised; and whoever's heart was otherwise will see that by which he becomes certain of the matter of the Rising and the resurrection, so he knows it with his heart and witnesses it with his eyes; and that is the turning about of hearts and eyes.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أعْمالُهم كَسَرابٍ بِقِيعَةٍ﴾ — "اَلْقِيعَةُ" is the plural of "قاعٍ", like "جارٍ" and "جِيرَةٌ". "اَلْقِيعَةُ" and "اَلْقاعُ" are the flat expanse of land in which there is no vegetation; the one who travels across it sees as though there were flowing water in it, and that is the mirage (al-sarāb). "اَلْآلُ" is like the mirage, except that it rises in the forenoon like water between heaven and earth. ﴿يَحْسَبُهُ الظَّمْآنُ ماءً﴾ — "يَحْسِبُهُ" and "يَحْسَبُهُ" are both permissible, and "اَلظَّمْآنُ" and "اَلظَّمانُ" are permissible, the latter by lightening the hamza; it is one who is intensely thirsty. It is said "ظَمِئَ الرَّجُلُ، يَظْمَأُ، ظَمَأً، فَهو ظَمْآنُ" (the man became thirsty …, so he is thirsty), like "عَطِشَ، يَعْطَشُ، عَطَشًا، فَهو عَطْشانُ".
His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا جاءَهُ لَمْ يَجِدْهُ شَيْئًا﴾, that is: until, when he comes to the mirage and to its place, he sees land with no water in it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the disbeliever thinks his deeds have benefited him with Allah — his thought is like the thought of one who thinks the mirage is water — while his deeds have come to nothing and gone. Allah struck this likeness for the disbeliever and said: the deeds of the disbelievers are like this mirage, ﴿أوْ كَظُلُماتٍ في بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ﴾ [al-Nūr: 40], to the end of the verse; because He, Mighty and Majestic is He, described His light which is for the believers, and made known that the hearts of the believers and their deeds are like the light which He described, and that they will find it with Allah, Who will reward them for it with Paradise; and that the deeds of the disbelievers, if likened to something that is found, their likeness is that of the mirage, and if likened to something that is seen, they are like these darknesses which He described in His saying: ﴿أوْ كَظُلُماتٍ في بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ﴾ [al-Nūr: 40], to the end of the verse.
His saying: ﴿إذا أخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَراها﴾ [al-Nūr: 40] — its meaning is: he did not see it, nor nearly [see it]. Some of them said: he sees it after not having seen it because of the intensity of the darkness. The first view is more fitting to this meaning, because in less than these darknesses the palm of the hand is not seen.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن لَمْ يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ لَهُ نُورًا فَما لَهُ مِن نُورٍ﴾ [al-Nūr: 40], that is: whomever Allah does not guide to Islam is not guided.

zajjaj:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ مَن في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ والطَّيْرُ صافّاتٍ﴾ — it is permissible to say "والطَّيْرَ" (accusative), in the sense of "the creation glorifies Him together with the birds", but it has not been read thus.
His saying: ﴿كُلٌّ قَدْ عَلِمَ صَلاتَهُ وتَسْبِيحَهُ﴾ — its meaning is: "each — Allah knows its prayer and its glorification"; prayer is for people and glorification is for other than people. It may be that "كُلٌّ قَدْ عَلِمَ صَلاتَهُ وتَسْبِيحَهُ" means "everything knows its own prayer and its glorification"; and it may mean "every human knows the prayer to Allah, and everything knows the glorification of Allah". The best is that it be "each — Allah knows its prayer and its glorification", and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿واللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِما يَفْعَلُونَ﴾.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ يُزْجِي سَحابًا﴾ — the meaning of "يُزْجِي" is: He drives. ﴿ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُ﴾, that is: He makes the scattered pieces of cloud into one piece. ﴿ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ رُكامًا﴾, that is: He makes some of the clouds mount upon others. ﴿فَتَرى الوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِن خِلالِهِ﴾ — "اَلْوَدْقُ" is the rain. It is also read "مِن خَلَلِهِ"; "خِلالِهِ" is more general and better in reading. "خِلالٌ" is the plural of "خَلَلٌ": "خَلَلٌ" and "خِلالٌ" are like "جَبَلٌ" and "جِبالٌ". "اَلسَّحابُ" may be the plural of "سَحابَةٌ", and "بَيْنَهُ" then means "between all of it"; and "اَلسَّحابُ" may be singular, except that He said "بَيْنَهُ" because of its abundance. You may not say "جَلَسْتُ بَيْنَ زَيْدٍ" (I sat between Zayd) until you say "وَعَمْرٍو" (and ʿAmr); but you say "ما زِلْتُ أدُورُ بَيْنَ الكُوفَةِ" (I kept going about between Kufa), because "اَلْكُوفَةُ" is a name that includes many places, so it is as though you said: "I kept going about between the roads of Kufa".
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيُنَـزِّلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ مِن جِبالٍ فِيها مِن بَرَدٍ﴾ — "وَيُنْزِلُ", without doubling, is permissible. The meaning of "مِنَ السَّماءِ مِن جِبالٍ فِيها مِن بَرَدٍ" is "from mountains of hail in it", as you say "هَذا خاتَمٌ في يَدِي مِن حَدِيدٍ" (this is a ring on my hand, of iron), the meaning being "هَذا خاتَمُ حَدِيدٍ في يَدِي" (this is an iron ring on my hand). It is also possible — and Allah knows best — that the meaning of "مِن جِبالٍ" is: from the amount of mountains of hail, as you say "عِنْدَ فُلانٍ جِبالُ مالٍ" (so-and-so has mountains of wealth), meaning "the amount of mountains", because of its abundance. His saying: ﴿يَكادُ سَنا بَرْقِهِ يَذْهَبُ بِالأبْصارِ﴾ — Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read "يُذْهِبُ بِالأبْصارِ", and no one else read it thus; its justification in Arabic is weak, because the speech of the Arabs is "ذَهَبْتُ بِهِ" and "أذْهَبْتُهُ" [not both together]; yet that too is permissible, I mean the ḍamma on the yāʾ in "يُذْهِبُ". The meaning of "سَنا بَرْقِهِ" is: the brightness of its lightning. It was also read "سَنا بُرْقِهِ يَذْهَبُ بِالأبْصارِ", as the plural of "بُرْقَةٌ": "بُرْقٌ". The difference between "بُرْقِهِ" with ḍamma and "بَرْقِهِ" with fatḥa is that "اَلْبَرْقُ" [Translator's note: so in the source; the explanation that follows suggests «اَلْبُرْقَةُ» with ḍamma is meant here] is the quantity of lightning, and "اَلْبُرْقَةُ" [Translator's note: likewise, «اَلْبَرْقَةُ» with fatḥa appears to be meant] is that a thing flashes a single time; as you say "غَرَفْتُ غَرْفَةً واحِدَةً" (I scooped a single scoop), meaning "a single time", while "اَلْغَرْفَةُ" [i.e. «الغُرْفَة»] is the quantity scooped; and likewise "اَللَّقْمَةُ" and "اَللُّقْمَةُ".

zajjaj:45-45.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿واللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دابَّةٍ مِن ماءٍ﴾ — it is also read "واللَّهُ خالِقُ كُلِّ دابَّةٍ مِن ماءٍ". "دابَّةٌ" is a name for every animal, rational and otherwise. Since it applies both to what has reason and to what does not, He said ﴿فَمِنهُمْ﴾; had it been for what has no reason, it would have been said "فَمِنها" or "مِنهُنَّ". Then He said ﴿مَن يَمْشِي عَلى بَطْنِهِ﴾, using "مَن", though "مَن" is originally for what has reason, because when He mixed the group and it was said "فَمِنهم", the expression was made with "مَن". And it was said "يَمْشِي عَلى بَطْنِهِ" (walks on its belly) because every moving creature, whether it has two legs, or four, or has no legs, is called "ماشٍ" (walker) and [it is said] "قَدْ مَشى" (it has walked); and everything that continues is called "ماشٍ", even if it is not an animal, so that it is said "قَدْ مَشى هَذا الأمْرُ" (this matter has proceeded). ﴿مِن ماءٍ﴾ — it was said "مِن ماءٍ" just as Allah, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا مِنَ الماءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 30].

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿وَإنْ يَكُنْ لَهُمُ الحَقُّ يَأْتُوا إلَيْهِ مُذْعِنِينَ﴾ — it came in the exegesis: "مُسْرِعِينَ" (hastening). "اَلْإذْعانُ" in the language is hastening together with obedience. You say "قَدْ أذْعَنَ لِي بِحَقِّي" (he has yielded my right to me), meaning: he has complied with me in what I was seeking from him, and has come hastening to it.

zajjaj:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ لا تُقْسِمُوا طاعَةٌ مَعْرُوفَةٌ﴾ — its interpretation is: "طاعَةٌ مَعْرُوفَةٌ أمْثَلُ مِن قَسَمِكم لِما لا تَصْدُقُونَ فِيهِ" (a recognised obedience is better than your swearing to what you are not truthful in). The khabar (predicate) is implied (muḍmar), namely "أمْثَلُ" (better), and it was omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech, since He said: ﴿وَأقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أيْمانِهِمْ لَئِنْ أمَرْتَهم لَيَخْرُجُنَّ﴾, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is beyond (i.e. aware of) what is in their hearts, so He said: ﴿قُلْ لا تُقْسِمُوا طاعَةٌ مَعْرُوفَةٌ إنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ﴾. "طاعَةً مَعْرُوفَةً" (accusative) is also permissible, in the sense of "أطِيعُوا طاعَةً مَعْرُوفَةً" (obey with a recognised obedience), because they swore that if they were commanded they would obey, so it was said: obey with a recognised obedience. But I do not know anyone who read it thus, and if it has not been transmitted, then do not read it. By this the hypocrites are meant.

zajjaj:55-55.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكم وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهم في الأرْضِ كَما اسْتَخْلَفَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ — the lām came only because "وَعَدْتُهُ بِكَذا أوْ كَذا" (I promised him such-and-such) and "وَعَدْتُهُ لَأُكْرِمَنَّهُ" (I promised him: I will surely honour him) are equivalent to "قُلْتُ" (I said), because a promise is concluded only by speech. The meaning of "لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهم في الأرْضِ" is: He will surely make them succeed those [who came] after them among the believers, as He made those before them successors. [Translator's note: the wording is as in the source.] It was also read: "كَما اسْتُخْلِفَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ" (passive). ﴿وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهم دِينَهُمُ الَّذِي ارْتَضى لَهُمْ﴾ — by it He means Islam. ﴿وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهم مِن بَعْدِ خَوْفِهِمْ أمْنًا﴾ — it was also read "وَلَيُبْدِلَنَّهم".
His saying: ﴿يَعْبُدُونَنِي لا يُشْرِكُونَ بِي شَيْئًا﴾ — it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), and it may be in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial), in the sense of "Allah promised the believers, in the state of their worship and their sincerity to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, that He would surely do [this] for them". It may also be a resumption by way of praising them and confirming [them], as if He said: "the believers worship Me, not associating anything with Me".

zajjaj:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿لا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مُعْجِزِينَ في الأرْضِ﴾ — the reading is with the tāʾ, in the sense of "do not think, O Muḥammad, that the disbelievers can escape [Allah]", that is: "the power of Allah encompasses them". It was also read "لا يُحْسَبَنَّ" [Translator's note: so in the source; the discussion that follows concerns the reading «لا يَحْسَبَنَّ» with yāʾ], with the first object of "يَحْسَبَنَّ" omitted, in the sense of "لا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إيّاهم مُعْجِزِينَ في الأرْضِ" (let not those who disbelieve think themselves able to escape in the earth), just as you say "زَيْدٌ حَسِبَهُ" [qāʾiman], by which you mean only "he thought himself standing"; so it is as though [it were] "لا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أنْفُسَهم مُعْجِزِينَ". This is in the category of "ظَنَنْتُ" (verbs of thinking), where "نَفْس" (self) is dropped: it is said "ظَنَنْتُنِي أفْعَلُ" (I thought myself doing), and it is not said "ظَنَنْتُ نَفْسِي أفْعَلُ"; whereas "ضَرَبْتُنِي" (I struck me) is not permissible — it is dispensed with by "ضَرَبْتُ نَفْسِي" (I struck myself).

zajjaj:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِيَسْتَأْذِنْكُمُ الَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم والَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا الحُلُمَ مِنكم ثَلاثَ مَرّاتٍ﴾ — Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded asking permission at the times when people are in private and uncovered, and He made them clear, saying: ﴿مِن قَبْلِ صَلاةِ الفَجْرِ وحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيابَكم مِنَ الظَّهِيرَةِ ومِن بَعْدِ صَلاةِ العِشاءِ﴾ — by this is meant al-ʿatama, the later ʿishāʾ. He made known that they are times of privacy (ʿawrāt), and said ﴿ثَلاثُ عَوْراتٍ لَكُمْ﴾, in the sense of "هي ثَلاثُ عَوْراتٍ لَكم" (they are three times of privacy for you). It was also read "ثَلاثَ عَوَراتٍ لَكم". The sukūn is more common because of the heaviness of the vowel with the wāw. You say "طَلْحَةٌ" and "طَلَحاتٌ", "جَمْرَةٌ" and "جَمَراتٌ"; and in "لَوْزَةٌ", "لَوَزاتٌ" with a vowel on the wāw is permissible, but the better is "لَوْزاتٌ". "ثَلاثَ عَوَراتٍ" in the accusative is permissible, in the sense of "لِيَسْتَأْذِنُوكم ثَلاثَ عَوَراتٍ", that is: "at the times of three [occasions of] privacy".
His saying: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكم ولا عَلَيْهِمْ جُناحٌ بَعْدَهُنَّ﴾, that is: there is no blame on you nor on them in their not asking permission after each of these times has passed.
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿طَوّافُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ — in the sense of "هم طَوّافُونَ عَلَيْكم" (they are going about among you).
His saying: ﴿بَعْضُكم عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾ — in the sense of "يَطُوفُ بَعْضُكم عَلى بَعْضٍ" (some of you go about among others).

zajjaj:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذا بَلَغَ الأطْفالُ مِنكُمُ الحُلُمَ فَلْيَسْتَأْذِنُوا﴾ — so the one who has reached puberty asks permission at all times, while the child and the slave ask permission at the three times of privacy.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿والقَواعِدُ مِنَ النِّساءِ اللاتِي لا يَرْجُونَ نِكاحًا﴾ — "اَلْقَواعِدُ" is the plural of "قاعِدَةٌ", which is the woman who has ceased (lit. sat back) from marriage. ﴿اللاتِي لا يَرْجُونَ نِكاحًا﴾, that is: they do not want it and do not hope for it. It was also said: those who have ceased menstruating. ﴿فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِنَّ جُناحٌ أنْ يَضَعْنَ ثِيابَهُنَّ غَيْرَ مُتَبَرِّجاتٍ بِزِينَةٍ﴾ — Ibn Masʿūd said: that they put aside the wrap (milḥafa) and the cloak (ridāʾ). ﴿وَأنْ يَسْتَعْفِفْنَ خَيْرٌ لَهُنَّ﴾, that is: that they do not put aside the cloak and the wrap is better for them than that they put it aside.

zajjaj:61-61.t:
His saying: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلى الأعْمى حَرَجٌ ولا عَلى الأعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ ولا عَلى المَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ﴾ — "اَلْحَرَجُ" in the language is narrowness, and its meaning in religion is sin. It came in the exegesis that the people of Medina, before the Prophet ﷺ was sent, would not eat together with these [people]. It was said that they did that for fear that the healthy would have the advantage over the food and these would have little opportunity, so it was said to them: there is no ḥaraj in eating together with them. It was said that they did that out of disgust. It was also said that when they went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ they would leave these behind, and they would feel it a sin to eat from what they were guarding, so they were informed that there is no blame on them. It was also said that some people would invite them to their food, and sometimes they would arrive at their homes and find no food in them, so they would take them on to their fathers. Everything they mentioned is good and sound, except what they mentioned of abandoning eating together out of disgust, for I do not know how that could be.
His saying: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكم جُناحٌ أنْ تَأْكُلُوا جَمِيعًا أوْ أشْتاتًا﴾ — the meaning of "أشْتاتًا" is: separately, individually; and "جَمِيعًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is related that there was a tribe of the Arabs among whom a man would not eat alone — they were a tribe of Kināna. A man would wait his whole day, and if he did not find someone to eat with him, he would eat nothing; and sometimes he would have with him camels ḥuffal, which are those whose udders are full of milk, and he would not drink of their milk until he found someone to drink with him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that if a man among them ate alone, there is no sin on him.
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَإذا دَخَلْتُمْ بُيُوتًا فَسَلِّمُوا عَلى أنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: "let some of you greet others", for Allah has commanded the greeting of peace. It was also said: "When you enter houses and they are empty, let the one entering say: Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah."
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَحِيَّةً مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ﴾ — its meaning: the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], because His saying "فَسَلِّمُوا" means "greet one another, and let some of you greet others, with a greeting from Allah". So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the greeting of peace is blessed and good.

zajjaj:62-62.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذا كانُوا مَعَهُ عَلى أمْرٍ جامِعٍ لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا حَتّى يَسْتَأْذِنُوهُ﴾ — some of them said: that was at the Friday prayer. It is — and Allah knows best — that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded the believers, when they were with His Prophet ﷺ in something that requires the community, such as war against the enemy, or something they attend that requires gathering, not to leave until they asked his permission. Likewise they ought to be with their imams: they do not oppose them nor turn away from them in any of their gatherings except with their permission; and the imam may grant permission or not grant it, according to what he sees of benefit in that, because of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَإذا اسْتَأْذَنُوكَ لِبَعْضِ شَأْنِهِمْ فَأْذَنْ لِمَن شِئْتَ مِنهُمْ﴾, so He made the choice in granting permission his. ﴿واسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمُ اللَّهَ﴾, that is: ask forgiveness for them for their leaving the community, if you see that they have an excuse.

zajjaj:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿لا تَجْعَلُوا دُعاءَ الرَّسُولِ بَيْنَكم كَدُعاءِ بَعْضِكم بَعْضًا﴾, that is: "do not say 'O Muḥammad' as one of you says to his companion, but say 'O Messenger of Allah' and 'O Prophet of Allah', with reverence, respect and lowered voice". Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known to them the superiority of the Prophet, upon him be peace, over all other creatures in the manner of address.
His saying: ﴿قَدْ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ يَتَسَلَّلُونَ مِنكم لِواذًا﴾ — the wāw is kept overt in "لِواذًا" according to [its being the maṣdar of] "لاوَذْتُ لِواذًا". The meaning of "لِواذًا" here is opposition, that is: they oppose [him] with opposition; and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿فَلْيَحْذَرِ الَّذِينَ يُخالِفُونَ عَنْ أمْرِهِ﴾. As for the maṣdar of "لُذْتُ", it is your saying "لُذْتُ بِهِ، لِياذًا" (I took refuge with him, a taking refuge).
